column1: # Every change the community patch repo applies to the Quest APK, mapped to what our build does instead (#1187).
# The patch repo is EchoTools/echoApkPatch (by marshmallow-mia), read at the commit on the next line. Nothing here is
# copied from it: `change` and `reason` are our words, and the YAML addresses and feature names are facts of its files.
#   source   the patch repo's tracked file the change is in
#   site     a YAML patch's address (ReVault's VA: the pinned vaddr + 0x100000), or an address a script writes; `feature` for a
#            disabled YAML feature; `file` for a file whose sites are rows of tools/quest_patcher_sites.tsv;
#            `@<text>` for a change inside a script (the text is in the file); `-` for the whole file
#   feature  the YAML feature name, exactly; otherwise a short label
#   change   what their change does, in our words
#   status   done (`ours` names our code), not_needed (the reason says why), open (`ours` names the issue that does
#            it), table (the file's sites are rows of tools/quest_patcher_sites.tsv)
#   ours     comma-separated: `<path>:<symbol>` in this tree, `#<issue>`, or `-`
#   reason   why the row's status holds
# tools/quest_apk_patch_map.py checks the table; with --repo it checks it against the patch repo's checkout.

column4: CSysFile::Init returns at once
column7: The mount is answered as done by a GOT hook on AStorageManager_mountObb (and the path by getMountedObbPath), so CSysFile::Init does not wait for an OBB the OS refuses; with no OBB file the function returns before the mount. On the reference build the function's first word is `ret`, so Init returns at once and the mount and path hooks are idle

column4: cave: texres trampolines and the one-time load of libtexres.so
column7: The cave holds three trampolines and loads a library. Ours has no cave and loads nothing: the eye size is a GOT hook on vrapi_GetSystemPropertyInt (texture_quality_hook.cpp), the settings are a GOT hook on ApplyRuntimeGfxSettings (HandleApply) and the resize check is a GOT hook on CheckForResize (HandleCheck); Install proves libr15 and installs them (docs/adr/0015)

column4: CEngine::RenderBefore: CheckForResize call -> texres check
column7: CEngine::CheckForResize is called through libr15's own PLT (one caller, RenderBefore), so a GOT hook on its slot is the call site: the handler runs the original, then the engine's own CVR::RefreshRTSize and CEngine::Resize (through the engine's resize slot) when a different level was asked for

column4: ApplyRuntimeGfxSettings entry -> texres settings
column7: ApplyRuntimeGfxSettings is called through libr15's own PLT, so a GOT hook on its slot is the entry: the handler reads graphics|msaa (SR15GfxSettings+0x1c) and asks for that level; the first delivery with nothing saved takes the configuration's level

column4: ValidateGfxSettings: msaa upper clamp -> nop
column7: ValidateGfxSettings is called through libr15's own PLT; its one clamp of the msaa field is min(msaa, 2). The handler puts the value the settings held back, clamped to the menu's 0..5, so six levels persist; no instruction is changed

column4: ApplyRuntimeGfxSettings: MSAA-mode debug log call -> nop
column7: The patch removes the dev log call "MSAA mode: %s" so index 3 to 5 cannot read past the three-entry name table. In the pinned libr15 the slots after the table (kMsaaNames, ELF 0x3690278) are ABS64 relocations to valid pointers (0x3690290, 0x3690298, 0x36902a0), so the call prints a wrong word for those indices and cannot fault; ours leaves the call and its cosmetic line alone (docs/adr/0015)
